net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
We derive the majority of our revenue from sales of our networking equipment, with the remaining revenues generated from sales of subscription and support, which primarily includes software subscriptions delivered as software as a service (“SaaS”) and additional revenues from maintenance contracts, professional services and training for the products we offer. We sell our products and SaaS and maintenance contracts direct to customers and to partners in two distribution channels, or tiers. The first tier consists of a limited number of independent distributors that stock our products and sell primarily to resellers. The second tier of the distribution channel consists of non-stocking distributors and value-added resellers that sell primarily to end-users. Products and services may be sold separately or in bundled packages.

We consider customer purchase orders, which in some cases are governed by master sales agreements, to be the contracts with a customer. For each contract, we consider the promise to transfer products and services, each of which are distinct, to be the identified performance obligations.

net sales.text:

We sell our products and SaaS and maintenance contracts direct to customers and to partners in two distribution channels, or tiers. The first tier consists of a limited number of independent distributors that stock our products and sell primarily to resellers. The second tier of the distribution channel consists of non-stocking distributors and value-added resellers that sell primarily to end-users. Products and services may be sold separately or in bundled packages.

We consider customer purchase orders, which in some cases are governed by master sales agreements, to be the contracts with a customer. For each contract, we consider the promise to transfer products and services, each of which are distinct, to be the identified performance obligations.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In fiscal 2026, sales to customers outside of the United States accounted for 55% of our consolidated net revenues, compared to 52% in fiscal 2025 and 48% in fiscal 2024.
Of these, 31.4% work in sales and marketing, 36.3% in research and development, 5.7% in operations, 14.4% in customer support and services and 12.2% in finance and administration.

Support revenues from maintenance contracts included in Subscription and support revenues but excluded from SaaS ARR were $235.3 million and $234.2 million, representing 49.6% and 53.8% of total Subscription and support revenues, respectively, for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

• We depend upon international sales for a significant portion of our revenues, which imposes a number of risks on our business.
We rely on many resellers worldwide that sell directly to the end-user customer.
Actual shipments of products depend on the then-current capacity of our contract manufacturers and the availability of materials and components from our vendors.
We also leverage and depend on the strong Environmental, Social and Governance policies and standards of our manufacturing partners.

Our products rely on key components, including merchant silicon, integrated circuit components and power supplies purchased from a limited number of suppliers, including certain sole source providers.

As we develop our product roadmap and continue to expand our relationships with these and other merchant silicon vendors, it is critical that we work in tandem with our key vendors to ensure that their silicon includes improved features and that our products take advantage of such improved features.

We believe that continued success in the marketplace relies on our ability to regularly bring to the market new and enhanced products employing leading-edge technology that provide business solutions affordably, securely, and effortlessly.
We rely on a combination of patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret laws and restrictions on disclosure to protect our intellectual property rights.
A substantial portion of our business depends on the demand for enterprise-scale networking, which, in turn, is impacted by the overall economic health of our current and prospective end-customers.

We primarily rely on our manufacturing partners Alpha Networks, Inc., Senao Networks, Inc., Wistron Neweb Corporation, Sercomm Corporation, Quanta Computer Inc., Lite-On Technology Corporation, and select other partners to manufacture our products.

Given the concentration of our supply chain, particularly with certain sole or limited source providers, any significant disruption to any of the key suppliers or a termination of a relationship could temporarily impact our operations and our ability to meet customer orders.

In particular, we rely on certain memory and semiconductor components that have experienced supply constraints, reduced production capacity, and significant price volatility as suppliers shift to newer technologies, resulting in increased costs, longer lead times, and potential allocation limitations that could adversely affect our ability to manufacture and deliver products.

Our ability to grow subscription revenue also depends on our ability to attract new subscribers, retain existing customers, expand adoption of subscription and cloud offerings, and maintain favorable renewal and attach rates, any of which may be adversely affected by competition, customer budget constraints, pricing pressures, or changes in customer preferences.
A number of our employees are foreign nationals who rely on visas and entry permits to legally work in the United States and other countries.
We rely on third-party providers for services needed to deliver our cloud solutions and other third-party providers for our internal operations.

We increasingly rely on third-party cloud providers, including AWS, GCP, and Azure, to host our cloud solutions and support a growing number of our products, services, and internal operations, including enterprise systems.
We also increasingly rely on third-party artificial intelligence technologies, including third-party models, tools, and platforms that may be integrated into our products or internal operations.
A portion of our sales to educational institutions depends on government funding programs, including E-Rate.
We rely on the availability of third-party licenses.

As of June 30, 2026, our principal sources of liquidity consisted of cash and cash equivalents of $211.8 million, accounts receivable, net of $164.6 million, and available borrowings under our 2023 Revolving Facility (as defined below) of $135.6 million.
